overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated YouTube Shorts performance data reveals clear audience preference for space and planetary 'What If' scenarios and extreme cosmic anomalies. Videos framed around speculative planetary conditions (e.g., liquid diamond planets, dark planets, and burning ice) consistently generate the highest view counts and engagement rates (likes-per-view) among recent 7-day uploads. Traditional static fact-stating underperforms compared to interactive, immersive thought experiments ('What If You Fell Into...'). Conversely, standard biological or psychological micro-facts from earlier weeks show lower traction unless paired with extreme comparative hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) dominate recent performance.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more hypothetical planetary survival and physics scenarios featuring extreme environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing bizarre weather or physical properties on distant worlds, such as 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (1,026 views) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views), outperform generic space facts.
winning_patterns.action: Focus hooks on unique, counter-intuitive physical phenomena in the universe using bold visual qualifiers.

weak_patterns.evidence: Older psychological and biological micro-facts like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) show negligible velocity.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tricks unless reframed into high-stakes or bizarre narrative formats.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve' (139 views) lag significantly behind the high-octane space survival content.
weak_patterns.action: Shift history and mystery concepts toward micro-storytelling or cinematic survival rather than dry factual summaries.

next_video.hook_style: What If scenario combining extreme physics with a vivid hypothetical death or survival situation
next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into a Star Made Entirely of Neon?
next_video.opening_direction: Start immediately with the visual plunge into a glowing neon-pink stellar ocean, asking what happens to the human body in the first microsecond.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that you wouldn't burn—you would instantly freeze and glow in the dark before being crushed by unimaginable pressure.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the proven high-performing 'What If' planetary and stellar hazard formula while introducing a fresh cosmic element (neon stars) not yet covered.
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not use diamond, coal, dark planet, or glass rain themes.
Must introduce a new celestial element/phenomenon.

experiment: A/B test a pure extreme fact hook ('This Star Glows Neon Pink') against a 'What If' survival hook ('What If You Fell Into a Neon Star?') using the same visual asset to confirm if hypothetical immersion drives higher initial viewer retention.
